:::{#thm-de-morgan-logic}
#### De Morgan's law for a conjunction

For any [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$
[@wikipedia_de_morgans_laws]:

$$
\neg (P \land Q) \equiv \neg P \lor \neg Q
$$

:::

::: proof

Each side is built from $P$ and $Q$,
so by @def-logically-equivalent
it is enough to compare the two sides in each of the four rows of a [truth table](#def-truth-table):

| $P$ | $Q$ | $\neg (P \land Q)$ | $\neg P \lor \neg Q$ |
|:---:|:---:|:------------------:|:--------------------:|
| T   | T   | F                  | F                    |
| T   | F   | T                  | T                    |
| F   | T   | T                  | T                    |
| F   | F   | T                  | T                    |

The third and fourth columns agree in every row.

:::
